precommit.name: PCBE-1 proof-carrying build expression
precommit.purpose: Certify deterministic build-like integer results from explicitly declared environment/configuration and dependency-digest premises without invoking a compiler, test runner, SMT solver, proof assistant, zkVM or hosted executor.
checker_rules: ENV(name) is valid only if name is present in certificate.declared_environment and evaluates to that declared integer.
ADD/SUB/MUL check both child proofs then apply exact integer arithmetic.
DIV_EXACT checks divisor != 0 and dividend mod divisor == 0 before integer division; otherwise reject.
DIGEST_EQ(name,d) is valid only if name is present in certificate.dependency_digests; it returns 1 iff the bound digest string equals d, else 0.
IF_EQ(a,b,t,e) checks proofs for a and b, then checks only the selected branch t if a==b else e; the certificate must identify the selected branch and its proof.
The root value must equal certificate.claimed_result.
Any ENV read not present in declared_environment rejects; any dependency name not present in dependency_digests rejects; there is no ambient/default environment lookup.

complexity_claim.scope: acyclic tree-form expressions only; no shared DAG nodes, recursion, loops, side effects or external calls
complexity_claim.proof_size: one proof record per checked AST node
complexity_claim.checker_work: one local rule check per proof record plus bounded map lookup/string comparison; O(number_of_checked_nodes + total_digest_string_length)
complexity_claim.basis: structural traversal of the precommitted grammar, not a runtime benchmark

precommit.critical_boundary: PCBE-1 proves a result conditional on declared premises. It does not measure an opaque physical machine/environment. If correctness depends on facts not already bound in readable inputs (actual CPU, installed toolchain, filesystem, network, timing, kernel behavior), discovering those facts remains an unresolved execution/measurement child.

tests.falsifies: Any certificate or source-only cache that reuses the result 42 after a relevant declared build flag changes.
Reusing a result after an explicitly bound dependency identity changes.

result.transversal_value: A single proof-carrying format can bind declared build flags, environment/configuration values, dependency identities and deterministic arithmetic/branch semantics, turning several compile/test-like checks into auditable finite derivations.
limits: No claim about actual ambient machine state unless that state is already represented by trusted/readable premise data.
No loops, recursion, shared-state concurrency or performance properties.
Digest strings are premises/identities; PCBE-1 does not itself hash arbitrary unreadable binary content.

next_tests: Add premise-origin tags distinguishing repository-identity facts, user-declared configuration and external observations; acceptance must reject unsupported external observations.
Test content-addressed artifact reuse where Git blob SHA is supplied as dependency identity and PCBE-1 proves a small selection rule without rebuilding.

Audit certifying compiler/proof-producing compiler literature for certificate formats that preserve the small-checker asymmetry while exposing whether fresh proof generation still needs unavailable execution.
